subject: POC scope & success criteria — Acme Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmecorp.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:09:00 -0800
Subject: POC scope & success criteria — Acme Corp

Thanks for the call today — great context, Sarah and Tom. Per our discussion, below is a concise recap and the proposed POC plan so we can get aligned on success criteria and timelines. Please reply with any changes by EOD Monday so we can finalize the SOW and start provisioning.

TL;DR POC goals:
- Validate Redwood Inference can meet Acme's customer-support summarization latency and quality targets for your 3M monthly messages workload.
- Confirm end-to-end integration with your anonymization pipeline and S3 storage for KV cache warmup.
- Measure cost per 1K tokens and determine production config (batching + quantization).

Success criteria (proposed):
1) Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 450ms for 1K prompt tokens (under expected concurrency profile).
2) Quality: ROUGE-L >= 0.58 on the provided support-thread test set + manual spot-check pass rate >= 88% on human review.
3) Integration: Automated nightly sync of sample dataset to our test S3 bucket + KV cache pre-warm runs succeed for 5/5 sample batches.
4) Cost: Demonstrated cost per 1K tokens within <= 1.3x of Redwood projected baseline for this workload.

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): Sign SOW, provide access (S3 creds, redacted sample set), security questionnaire.
- Week 1: Platform provisioning, initial integration test, ingest sample data.
- Week 2: Run baseline evals, enable caching & batching, iterate on prompt templates.
- Week 3: Final evaluation, review metrics, go/no-go decision.

Owners:
- Redwood: Marissa (sales/eng coordination), Camila (integration lead), Rishi (runtime/latency owner).
- Acme: Sarah (project sponsor), Tom (eng lead).

Attachments: attached draft SOW (POC_SOW_v2.pdf) and the completed security questionnaire (security_questionnaire_filled.xlsx).

Next steps:
1) Acme: confirm success criteria and share S3 read creds + sample dataset by Monday EOD.
2) Redwood: finalize SOW and send DocuSign link once criteria confirmed.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acmecorp.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC scope & success criteria — Acme Corp

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A couple of updates from our side after internal alignment: we want to add a second use case into the POC scope — short-form email reply suggestion for high-volume categories (about 250k messages/month). This is adjacent to summarization but has slightly different success criteria (precision on suggested replies, and acceptable latency target up to 600ms P95).

Implication: we understand this increases the surface area. Two asks:
1) Can Redwood confirm this is feasible within the same POC window (or propose a re-baseline timeline)?
2) Can we add one additional evaluation metric for reply suggestion: Top-1 accuracy on a labeled sample >= 82%?

We'll still provide the same integration touchpoints (S3, anonymized sample sets). If this changes cost estimates materially, we should capture that before sign.

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Lee
Director, Product Ops | Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmecorp.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC scope & success criteria — Acme Corp

Sarah — appreciate the prompt follow-up and the clarity on the additional use case. Quick answer: we can support adding the reply-suggestion use case, but we should re-baseline scope and timing to keep the POC reliable and measurable. Proposed adjustments below — please confirm so we can finalize the SOW and updated DocuSign.

Updated success criteria (additions in italics):
- Reply suggestion: Top-1 accuracy >= 82% (on Acme-labeled set), Latency P95 <= 600ms.
- Summarization criteria remain as-is.

Re-baselined timeline (two-track approach):
- Week 0: Sign updated SOW, provide two labeled sample sets (summarization + reply suggestions).
- Week 1: Provisioning + integration for both tracks; Redwood to run a lightweight smoke test for both models.
- Week 2: Run parallel evals for summarization and reply suggestion; iterate on prompts and sampling.
- Week 3: Final metrics review and cost bake-off; go/no-go.

Operational notes and risks:
- Engineering note: reply suggestion requires slightly different prompt templates and an augmented evaluation harness; this will add ~3 engineer-days during Week 1-2.
- Cost: we estimate a +10-15% delta on token-processing costs due to separate evaluation runs; we will share an updated cost table once we have the labeled sample sizes.

If that plan looks reasonable, we will: 1) update the SOW and push a revised DocuSign link, 2) provision an additional evaluation folder in the Drive, and 3) schedule a 30-minute sync (Week 0) to hand off creds and answer engineering questions.

Camila/Rishi — can you confirm engineering availability for the extra 3 engineer-days and whether we need to push any timelines?

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -0800

Hey team — quick update from engineering after I scoped the changes: we can absorb the additional work within our current sprint if we prioritize the POC tasks. I estimate 2.5 engineer-days total (Rishi and I will split work). No infra changes required; we'll reuse the same GPU pool but will run additional parallel eval jobs which increases run-time cost.

I attached a short runbook for the parallel eval orchestration (runbook_parallel_eval.txt) — sending as an attachment stub here for reference.

Camila
